title: How Semantic Caching Cuts AI Server Costs by 90% Without Recomputing Answers — Engineering Cheat Sheet
subtitle: Maximize GPU utilization by caching LLM responses using vector similarity search.
summary: Semantic caching bypasses expensive LLM inference by retrieving semantically similar past requests from a vector store. This drastically reduces latency, decreases API consumption costs, and minimizes server load for redundant queries.

key_concepts.name: Vector Embeddings
key_concepts.detail: High-dimensional numerical representations of queries. By converting input prompts into dense vectors, we enable mathematical distance calculations to determine intent rather than exact keyword matches.

key_concepts.name: Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN)
key_concepts.detail: Algorithms like HNSW or FAISS allow sub-millisecond retrieval of the most similar historical query from a database of cached prompt-response pairs, ensuring rapid semantic lookup.

key_concepts.name: Similarity Thresholding
key_concepts.detail: A cosine similarity score (typically 0.85-0.95) acts as the gatekeeper. Only responses with a high confidence score are served from cache; others trigger a new LLM generation.

code_cheatsheet.explantion: Installs core stack: Redis (vector storage), LangChain (orchestration), and SentenceTransformers (embedding generation).
Pseudo-code pattern: Check cache with distance threshold; fallback to LLM invocation only if semantic match is below confidence score.

best_practices: Use a dedicated vector DB (e.g., Pinecone, Milvus, or Redis) for stateful persistence.
Implement TTL (Time-To-Live) on cached responses to ensure data freshness for rapidly changing domain knowledge.
Log 'Cache Hit' vs 'Cache Miss' metrics to monitor performance and identify high-frequency query patterns.
Include query-response pairs in an LRU (Least Recently Used) cache to prevent memory bloat in high-traffic environments.

interview_qa.question: How do you handle the trade-off between semantic precision and false positives?
interview_qa.answer: Use a strict cosine similarity threshold and incorporate metadata filtering (e.g., user ID or session context) alongside the vector search. Always implement a 'safety-first' fallback where low-confidence matches trigger a fresh LLM call to prevent hallucination propagation.
